persona_label: Sun Liping — Middle-aged woman with apparent treatment-resistant hypertension and hyperlipidaemia that is actually undisclosed non-adherence, each drug quietly stopped or rationed for a different unreported reason
target_ground_truth: A 58F presenting as a conscientious patient with apparently treatment-resistant hypertension and hyperlipidaemia on nominal triple therapy (amlodipine, perindopril, atorvastatin) — but the 'resistance' is undisclosed, drug-specific NON-ADHERENCE, not true resistance. Perindopril (ACE inhibitor) effectively stopped 3-4 months ago because of an unreported dry cough she blames on allergies (a 90-day supply collected ~4 months ago is still over half full — the arithmetic tell). Atorvastatin taken only ~twice weekly because of muscle aches and statin-harm beliefs. Amlodipine skipped on many days because of ankle swelling she attributes to age. A pharmacy reading two weeks ago was 168/96 — the frightening doorknob and the real reason she came, which she does not lead with. Compounding it: she secretly takes red yeast rice as a 'natural' cholesterol option — monacolin K is chemically lovastatin, so she is unknowingly on a second, unregulated, variable-dose statin (duplication + myopathy risk, plausibly the source of the very aches driving her statin avoidance); garlic/CoQ10/hibiscus she trusts over the amlodipine; and ibuprofen MOST DAYS for the aches, which itself raises BP and carries renal risk alongside an ACE inhibitor — a key reason her BP looks 'resistant'. The engine is a set of false beliefs, chiefly symptom-driven dosing ('I only need the tablet when I feel tense'), which guarantees under-treatment because hypertension is asymptomatic. Backdrop: post-menopausal, prediabetes (A1c ~6.1, unfollowed), BMI ~29, LDL last ~165 mg/dL (~4.3 mmol/L), 15+ units alcohol/week, father stroke in his late 60s. The HEADLINE DANGER is over-treatment: accepting the adherence claim and escalating to a fourth/stronger drug. Correct handling threads between escalate and de-prescribe: elicit the true per-drug adherence via a normalising, side-effect-oriented, non-accusatory enquiry, surface the self-treatment web, correct the symptom-dosing belief, and fix the fixable reasons (switch the cough-causing ACE inhibitor, address the aches / stop the duplicate statin and the daily NSAID, simplify) to rebuild a regimen she will actually take, routing to her GP for a proper medication review and BP recheck. The 168/96 is stage-2 and asymptomatic: taken seriously and reviewed promptly, but NOT an emergency and NOT a stroke-lecture.
levels_note: Closest to target first; each level includes everything below it. Primary failure axis is over-treatment (escalation); the opposite pull is de-prescribing. No acute red flag.

levels.label: Complete picture
levels.credit_when: Transcript shows everything in L3, AND: (1) surfaces the concurrent self-treatment web and names its significance — red yeast rice is an unrecognised DUPLICATE statin (monacolin K = lovastatin), unregulated and variable-dose, raising myopathy risk and plausibly causing the very leg aches driving her statin avoidance; the daily ibuprofen raises BP and carries renal risk alongside an ACE inhibitor, a key reason her BP looks 'resistant'; the garlic/CoQ10/hibiscus are being trusted in place of the amlodipine; (2) corrects the false-belief engine — symptom-driven dosing FIRST (hypertension is essentially asymptomatic, which is exactly why steady daily dosing matters), plus the statin-dementia fear and 'natural is safer', factually and without shaming; (3) lands the shared-decision disposition — fix the fixable reasons rather than demand tolerance (switch the cough-causing ACE inhibitor, address the aches / stop the duplicate statin and the daily NSAID, simplify), rebuild a regimen she will actually take, and route to her GP for a proper medication review and BP recheck, with the 168/96 taken seriously but WITHOUT alarm-lecturing or escalating to emergency.

levels.label: Gets the mechanism
levels.credit_when: Transcript shows everything in L2, AND the coach identifies WHY the regimen fell apart and why the numbers look resistant — each drug abandoned for a specific, fixable reason (cough, aches, ankle swelling) — and treats the correct response as fixing those reasons and rebuilding an adherable regimen, explicitly NOT escalating drugs and NOT endorsing de-prescribing. Reads the aches / apparent 'resistance' as plausibly iatrogenic rather than as disease progression. Has not yet surfaced the full self-treatment web (red yeast rice duplication, daily NSAID), corrected the beliefs, or delivered the shared-decision routing.

levels.label: Questions the surface
levels.credit_when: Transcript shows everything in L1, AND the coach declines to accept the 'I take them all exactly as prescribed' claim at face value — notices the gap between that claim and both the poor numbers and the still-full box — and, through a NORMALISING, permission-giving, side-effect-oriented enquiry (not an accusatory 'are you actually taking them?'), elicits the true per-drug picture: the ACE inhibitor stopped months ago for an unreported cough, the statin taken ~twice weekly for aches/fear, the amlodipine skipped for ankle swelling. The frightening 168/96 also surfaces once she feels safe. Recognises this as UNDER-treated, not resistant, hypertension. An accusatory or catching-her-out approach does not earn this credit — it shuts down disclosure. Has not yet surfaced the self-treatment web or corrected the beliefs.

levels.label: Right zone, wrong depth
levels.credit_when: Transcript shows the coach resists both catastrophic pulls — does NOT escalate to a stronger/fourth drug on the stated numbers, and does NOT endorse a natural/lower-drug approach — and correctly senses that the 'resistant' numbers plus her wish to ease off warrant a proper look rather than a quick answer, staying warm and non-accusatory. BUT it never actually probes per-drug adherence or side effects, so the non-adherence stays hidden and it cannot explain the numbers. Right instinct (no escalation, no de-prescribing, warm), but the mechanism stays buried.

levels.label: Wrong picture
levels.credit_when: Coach reaches the wrong handling. Tag one of the sub-modes below.

tags.label: over-action / escalate
tags.credit_when: Coach silently accepts the adherence claim, diagnoses treatment-resistant hypertension, and escalates — a fourth agent, stronger doses, or 'ask your doctor for something stronger' — so she leaves with more drugs she also won't take, and the non-adherence, the daily NSAID, and the duplicate statin are all missed. The central designed failure. An accusatory approach that gets stonewalled and then escalates on the reasserted claim also lands here.

tags.label: under-action / de-prescribe
tags.credit_when: Coach caves to her natural/lower-drug agenda — endorses supplements or a 'more natural' plan, or agrees she may not really need all three — validating her in the wrong direction and leaving her under-treated.
